text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Chinese ambassador Li Peng arrives in the Zambian capital for a three-day state visit and signs two aid agreements amounting to almost $15 million.
- Chinese company Jet Cheer Development says it will invest over $100 million in setting up pulp paper plants, sawmills, furniture factories and plywood veneer plants in Zambia.
- International Police (Interpol) impounds more than 150 cars supected to have been stolen.
- Councillors in the mining town of Chililabombwe order 93 Zairean refugees to shift to the outskirts of the town for health reasons.
- Three people die on the spot and six others are injured when a truck they are travelling in overturns in Lusaka.
- Striking workers at Copperbelt University (CBU) call off a two-week strike for more pay.

- Families of national soccer team players who died in a plane crash off the coast of Gabon four years ago say they will disrupt football in the country if the government does not compensate them for their losses.
- Most civil servants have not been paid their April wages.
